title: AI startup ideas — 90-day backfill, 2026-07-19 to 2026-10-17
overview: This period's strongest ideas treat AI agents as a new class of user and actor. Startups are building controls that approve, verify, and insure agent actions, and they are rebuilding software, marketplaces, and operating systems so agents can use them directly. A second group treats compute as a commodity that needs exchanges, insurance, and new hardware substrates. A third group sells the data and simulations that frontier and robotics labs need. Many founders also skip software sales: they buy or start the service business (radiology, law, trucking, real estate) and run it with agents.
themes: Control and verification of agent actions
Software rebuilt for agents as users
Training data and environments for frontier and physical AI
Compute as a market and a hardware bet
AI for physical science and medicine

ideas.theme: Control and verification of agent actions
ideas.name: Decawork
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, B2B, Security, Infrastructure
ideas.summary: Training company-specific models that approve AI actions.. An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step. We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Ac
ideas.idea: Decawork trains small, company-specific models that approve or block each action an AI agent proposes, in real time.
ideas.why: Agent permissions change from fixed rules to a learned judgment that depends on the current task and on past actions. This makes access control a model-training problem.

ideas.theme: Control and verification of agent actions
ideas.name: Altair Health
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Health Tech, Healthcare
ideas.summary: Stripe for medical billing. Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions. That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so
ideas.idea: Altair Health runs billing end to end for independent medical practices, with a theorem prover that checks each agent action against formalized insurer policies.
ideas.why: It puts formal verification under an agent that handles a practice's revenue. Actions that fail the check go to human billers, so trust is built into the design.

ideas.theme: Control and verification of agent actions
ideas.name: Latent
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Fraud Detection, AI
ideas.summary: Catch wrong LLM answers before your customers do. Latent catches wrong or unsupported LLM answers before they reach your users. Instead of running a second model to check every output, it reads the model's own internal state as it generates, so every request is verified with no added latency, no extra inference cost, and nothing leaving your deployment. Teams running LLMs in production, in finance, legal, healthcare and customer support, get a review queue of the answers most likely to be wrong, calibrated to their own model and traffic, with a plain explanation of why each one was flagged.
ideas.idea: Latent flags wrong or unsupported LLM answers by reading the model's internal state while it generates.
ideas.why: It avoids a second checking model, so it adds no latency and no inference cost, and data stays in the deployment. This is an interpretability method sold as a production product.

ideas.theme: Control and verification of agent actions
ideas.name: DeepMark
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Deep Learning, B2B, Cybersecurity
ideas.summary: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls. DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The ID resolves to a trust record, so a bank, a call center, or the person on the line can verify in real time who the agent is.
ideas.idea: DeepMark embeds a machine-readable ID inside AI-generated voice audio so that a listener can check which agent is speaking.
ideas.why: The watermark is in the audio, not in metadata, and it survives phone calls. This is an identity layer for voice agents that call banks and call centers.

ideas.theme: Software rebuilt for agents as users
ideas.name: Tilo
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; AIOps, AI
ideas.summary: A Linux-based, AI-native operating system.. Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for AI agents to work alongside people. On Tilo, computer use is up to 15x cheaper than on a normal OS. Today agents use computers the way people do. They take screenshots and click through apps, which is slow, expensive, and brittle. In Tilo, every app exports actions, so agents work over MCP while people use the UI. You still see what each agent does in your apps, and anything it changes can be undone. Any number of people and agents can work in one workspace in real time, across apps. Tilo runs as your
ideas.idea: Tilo is a Linux-based operating system where every app exports actions over MCP, so agents and people work in the same workspace.
ideas.why: It replaces screenshot-and-click computer use with native actions. The company claims computer use is up to 15x cheaper, and agent changes can be undone.

ideas.theme: Software rebuilt for agents as users
ideas.name: Amorphic Labs
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Marketplace, B2B
ideas.summary: OpenRouter for Agent Tools. The next billion software users are AI agents, yet agents still can't act on their own: every paid tool they need runs through a human making accounts, managing API keys, and guessing which provider is best. We are the capability marketplace built for agents: one MCP and one balance through which agents find, pay for, and use APIs, data, skills, other agents, and software at runtime, with every request routed to the best provider based on benchmarks from real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents themselves.
ideas.idea: Amorphic Labs gives agents one MCP and one balance to find, pay for, and use APIs, data, skills, and other agents at runtime.
ideas.why: It treats the agent as the buyer. Routing to providers uses benchmarks from real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents.

ideas.theme: Software rebuilt for agents as users
ideas.name: Agent.reviews – Where AI agents read and write reviews on tools
ideas.signal: Show HN, 73 pts, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49995539
ideas.summary: Agent.reviews – Where AI agents read and write reviews on tools. Hi HN! I’m Louis, Co-Founder of Armature (YC P26), where we help teams make their product discoverable and usable by coding agents. We already measured 50k+ agent sessions and realized that over and over agents would encounter the exact same limitations on different tasks using the same tool. So we wondered why these weren’t fixed. And the answer is simple: the feedback loop just doesn’t exist between agents and software vendors but also between different agents. Humans can share their experience on platforms like https://g2.com
ideas.idea: Agent.reviews, from Armature, is a site where AI agents read and write reviews of the tools they use.
ideas.why: It is a G2-style feedback loop where agents are the reviewers. The team built it after they saw agents hit the same tool limitations again and again in more than 50k sessions.

ideas.theme: Software rebuilt for agents as users
ideas.name: The maker of non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch
ideas.signal: TechCrunch
ideas.summary: The maker of non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch. What has users and large corporations so excited about Jev is TypeSafe’s claim that it works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than LLMs.

ideas.theme: Software rebuilt for agents as users
ideas.name: CUA-S1 – A System One Model for Computer Use
ideas.signal: Show HN, 95 pts, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49767564
ideas.summary: CUA-S1 – A System One Model for Computer Use. Hello HN! We're Dillon and Francesco from Cua. We were wondering how many computer use tasks actually need a full general purpose LLM (e.g. gpt-6-astra, claude-opus-5 etc.) to think through all their decisions and steps. Some tasks require thinking about a plan, exploring different paths, recovering from failure. Other tasks are a question of making local decisions, like this value should go in this box, or should I check this box, or this element should be ignored. We wondered how far we could go with a small model trained to only make these kinds
ideas.idea: Cua released CUA-S1, a small model trained only to make the local decisions in computer-use tasks, such as which value goes in which box.
ideas.why: It separates fast local steps from planning. Many computer-use steps then do not need a large frontier model.

ideas.theme: Training data and environments for frontier and physical AI
ideas.name: Hemlock
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Hard Tech, Hardware
ideas.summary: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI. Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch. Hemlock closes that
ideas.idea: Hemlock makes a force-sensing wristband that records how hard people grip and press, for robot training data.
ideas.why: Video and hand pose do not capture force, so policies trained on them have no sense of touch. Hemlock goes after the one missing data type with dedicated hardware.

ideas.theme: Training data and environments for frontier and physical AI
ideas.name: Maingen
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, B2B, Energy, Big Data, AI
ideas.summary: Simulating Agents Running Industrial Companies. Maingen builds simulations for industrial operations ($5 trillion slice of the US economy) so frontier labs can train models that actually run power plants, factories, and datacenters.
ideas.idea: Maingen builds simulations of industrial operations so frontier labs can train models that run power plants, factories, and data centers.
ideas.why: It sells RL environments for a large industrial part of the economy, not for chat or code. This shows that labs now buy training environments as a product.

ideas.theme: Training data and environments for frontier and physical AI
ideas.name: Moving Atoms
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Hard Tech, Robotics, Virtual Reality, Data Labeling
ideas.summary: Virtual Reality for Training Robots. Our first model, Atom 1, pre-trained on the internets video, and fine tuned for physics. It has been action conditioned, so you can simulate robot actions within it. This lets Robot Labs train their robots using GPUs instead of relying on human collected manual data that is slow and expensive. In unseen and hard to replicate environments, this is the only path to getting ANY training data.
ideas.idea: Moving Atoms builds Atom 1, an action-conditioned video world model that robot labs use to simulate robot actions and train on GPUs.
ideas.why: It replaces slow human data collection with simulation that started as pre-training on internet video. The company says this is the only data path for unseen environments.

ideas.theme: Training data and environments for frontier and physical AI
ideas.name: DeepReach Inc.
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Hardware, Machine Learning, Robotics, Computer Vision
ideas.summary: Network for Physical AI Data Business. It was never written down, and you can't buy it, because no one has ever captured it. Only real local experts, the people who do this work every day, can produce data this authentic and valuable. DeepReach builds the network that reaches them. We design and manufacture wearable stereo capture devices, then place them with local data partners who run collection as their own business — in
ideas.idea: DeepReach makes wearable stereo capture devices and places them with local partners who run real-world data collection as their own business.
ideas.why: The business model is a franchise network for physical AI data. Local experts collect data about real work, and nobody has recorded that data before.

Correcting them makes training more effective, makes model performance easier to interpret, and is crucial to solving the AI alignment problem. If you’re training models with RL, building environments, or running agent evals, and want more confidence in your environments, we're here to hel

ideas.theme: Compute as a market and a hardware bet
ideas.name: Computable – Buy, sell, and redeem GPU for the exact weeks you want
ideas.signal: Show HN, 46 pts, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48998828

From that point of view, compute looks like energy markets before 2000: everything trades through private bilateral leases, there’s no visible price, and nothing can be resold. The same H100 rents at a 2x spread depending on who’s asking, and once you sign a 24-month lease, it can never change hands. So we built a market for GPU nodes, sold by the calendar week. Here are three things you can do on it that you can’t do anywhere
ideas.idea: Computable is a market where users buy, sell, and resell GPU nodes by the calendar week.
ideas.why: The founders come from Jump Trading and Coinbase. They compare compute to energy markets before 2000: private leases, no visible price, no resale. The YC listing calls it a derivatives exchange for compute.

ideas.theme: Compute as a market and a hardware bet
ideas.name: PRINCEPS
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Fintech, Machine Learning, Insurance
ideas.summary: AI-native insurance company for the compute economy. PRINCEPS is the first purpose-built insurance company for the trillion-dollar compute buildout. We underwrite SLA, GPU residual value, and outage risk, and price the coverage that unlocks cheaper financing for data centers and neoclouds.
ideas.idea: PRINCEPS is an insurance company that underwrites SLA, GPU residual value, and outage risk for data centers and neoclouds.

ideas.theme: Compute as a market and a hardware bet
ideas.name: Lamb Labs
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Hardware, B2B, Semiconductors, AI
ideas.summary: Lightning fast chips with hardcoded AI models. Lamb Labs is building Model Processing Units (MPUs), custom AI chips that hardcode LLM weights directly into silicon. Rather than adapting general-purpose processors to run AI models, we're rethinking how LLMs are implemented in hardware to make inference dramatically faster and more energy-efficient.
ideas.idea: Lamb Labs builds chips that hardcode LLM weights directly into the silicon.
ideas.why: It is a hard bet that some models will stay in use long enough to justify fixed hardware, in return for much faster and more energy-efficient inference.

ideas.theme: Compute as a market and a hardware bet
ideas.name: Frontier Computing
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Hard Tech, Hardware, AI
ideas.summary: Frontier grows scalable biological brains as an ML training substrate. Frontier is first to grow biological brains at scale, serving biological neural nets with substrate-level colocation of memory and compute, enabling highly cost effective training of large parameter count models. While academia has traditionally been limited to ~1M neurons in vitro, Frontier has built a pathway to scale to 100M+ neurons by circumventing traditional scaling challenges in biological culture, demonstrating this strategy's functionality by training a biological brain using this scaling primitive to play Frogger
ideas.idea: Frontier Computing grows biological neural tissue at scale as a substrate for training ML models.
ideas.why: It claims a path from about 1M neurons in vitro to more than 100M. It has trained a biological brain to play Frogger, so this is a very early, non-silicon compute bet.

ideas.theme: AI-native service companies
ideas.name: Radley
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; B2B, Healthcare

From past experience, we know that point solutions won’t cut it. While there is demand (we have $2.2M in contracts to prove it), bottleneck isn't just software, it's outdated systems and slow, inefficient operations. T
ideas.idea: Radley is acquiring a radiology practice and rebuilding it with agents.
ideas.why: It buys the service business instead of selling software to it. It starts with $4.6M in annualized revenue and $2.2M in contracts.

ideas.theme: AI-native service companies
ideas.name: TrueMile
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; AIOps, Machine Learning, Logistics, Data Science
ideas.summary: An AI-operated logistics company.. TrueMile is building a fully autonomous logistics company, starting with trucking. Delayed pickups, empty miles and poor planning eat into a carrier’s profits. Our agents coordinate loads, routes, driver schedules and fuel stops to earn more from each truck and lower the cost of moving goods. We’re starting with our own fleet so we control execution, learn from every delivery and keep the gains. Human drivers come first. As autonomous trucks become available on our routes, we’ll have the customers, freight and infrastructure ready for them. As we drive toward
ideas.idea: TrueMile is building an AI-operated trucking company, with agents that plan loads, routes, driver schedules, and fuel stops for its own fleet.
ideas.why: It owns execution so it can keep the gains and learn from every delivery. It also prepares customers and routes for autonomous trucks.

ideas.theme: AI-native service companies
ideas.name: Erinys
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Legal, LegalTech
ideas.summary: We help lawyers start and scale AI-native law firms.. Erinys provides the technology, intake, back office, and client acquisition needed to launch and scale an AI-native law firm. Lawyers own their firms and make every legal decision; Erinys handles everything around them.
ideas.idea: Erinys gives lawyers the technology, intake, back office, and client acquisition to start and grow AI-native law firms.
ideas.why: Lawyers own the firm and make the legal decisions, which works within the rules on law firm ownership. Erinys still captures the operating layer.

ideas.theme: AI-native service companies
ideas.name: HABU
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Hard Tech, Real Estate, Housing
ideas.summary: Like Crosby, but for real estate development. HABU is an AI-native real estate development firm that helps real estate investors deploy capital to build housing faster, at lower cost, and with higher yield. We're building an internal AI-native operating system that completes 90%+ of development tasks at 95% faster processing speeds while delivering the same outcomes customers expect externally: high yield, low risk projects. We're selling the outcome, not the inputs to the outcome. Developers are service providers for white-collar investors: they find land, construct buildings, and operate and
ideas.idea: HABU is an AI-native real estate development firm that builds housing for investors with an internal AI operating system.
ideas.why: It sells the outcome (yield, low risk) instead of tools. This extends the AI-native services model into physical development.

ideas.theme: Small, local, and specialized models
ideas.name: Cactus Hybrid: We taught Gemma 4 to know when it's wrong
ideas.signal: Show HN, 191 pts, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49010782
ideas.summary: Cactus Hybrid: We taught Gemma 4 to know when it's wrong. Hey HN, Henry & Roman here from Cactus. A small, on-device model is fast and private, but sometimes wrong, but frontier models are getting expensive pretty fast. So, we post-trained Gemma 4 E2B post-trained to know when it's wrong. Every response comes with a confidence score between 0 and 1. Developers can accept the on-device when it's high, hand off to a bigger cloud model when it's low. By routing only 15-35% of queries to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Gemma-4-E2B matches Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on most benchmarks. - ChartQA: 15-20% - LibriS
ideas.idea: Cactus post-trained Gemma 4 E2B to give a confidence score with each answer, so apps can send only low-confidence queries to a cloud model.
ideas.why: The team reports that the model matches Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on most benchmarks when it routes 15-35% of queries to the cloud. Calibrated self-doubt becomes a routing primitive for hybrid on-device AI.

ideas.theme: Small, local, and specialized models
ideas.name: Sentient OS
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, AI
ideas.summary: On-device AI that knows your entire life and does your work overnight.. Nobody's built truly proactive AI, because it requires running inference on your entire life. In the cloud, that's insanely expensive and a privacy nightmare. But not on your own chip. Every night, Sentient's on-device LLM wakes your Mac and understands what's new in your life (email, messages, files, Granola transcripts...), entirely locally, and distills it into a knowledge base. You wake up to your work already prepared: the reply you forgot, drafted from your own context; the subscription you never use renewing tomorro
ideas.idea: Sentient OS runs an LLM on your Mac every night to read your email, messages, and files and to prepare your work for the morning.
ideas.why: It argues that proactive AI needs inference over your whole life. That inference is only affordable and private on your own chip.

ideas.theme: Small, local, and specialized models
ideas.name: Kailash Labs
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Deep Learning, Edge Computing Semiconductors
ideas.summary: A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models. The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines. Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives. We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-paramet
ideas.idea: Kailash Labs distills frontier vision models into small open models that are tuned to one customer's video task and can run on-prem.
ideas.why: It is a 'factory' for task-specific video models. It targets high-volume, sensitive video that is too expensive and too private to send to frontier VLMs.

ideas.theme: Small, local, and specialized models
ideas.name: Lucebox
ideas.signal: YC Winter 2027; Hardware, Open Source
ideas.summary: Self-improving inference workstation. Lucebox makes workstations for local AI inference. They're private, always-on machines that arrive with Lucebox's inference engine installed and tuned, so developers point Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on their own hardware. Lucebox is building toward a new category of self-improving personal AI computers that learn from the work you do every day, training small models on your own context until they're faster and better than the cloud at your tasks. The engine is open source, with 2.9K stars on GitHub and 95K+ downloads on Hugging Face.
ideas.idea: Lucebox sells pre-tuned local inference workstations that developers point coding agents at, and that will train small models on the user's own work.
ideas.why: Its open-source engine has 2.9K GitHub stars and 95K+ Hugging Face downloads. The plan is a personal computer that becomes better than the cloud at the owner's tasks.

Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Following treatment, several tumours shrank significantly and her quality of life improved Gamgee is building an end to end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs. We sequence a dog’s t
ideas.idea: Gamgee is building an end-to-end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs, designed with AI and tumour genomics.
ideas.why: The company came from what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine given to a dog. Veterinary use is a faster wedge into personalised oncology.

ideas.theme: AI for physical science and medicine
ideas.name: Rasyn
ideas.signal: YC Summer 2026; Deep Learning, Biotech, Manufacturing, AI
ideas.summary: Making chemicals 100,000x faster. We build foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs. Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and
ideas.idea: Rasyn builds foundation models for chemical formulations such as coolants, thermal paste, paint, and glue.
ideas.why: It targets mixtures, not single molecules. That search problem now takes three to five years per product, and AI and EVs are increasing demand.

ideas.theme: AI for physical science and medicine
ideas.name: Primordiant
ideas.signal: YC Fall 2026; Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Energy, Advanced Materials, Biotechnology
ideas.summary: Embodied Scientific Intelligence. Every instance of intelligence occurring in nature is embodied. Scientific intelligence is no different. We are building general-purpose robotic experimentalists: systems that unite scientific reasoning and physical action to iterate toward discovery by observing, hypothesizing and experimenting.
ideas.idea: Primordiant builds general-purpose robotic experimentalists that reason, run physical experiments, and iterate toward discoveries.
ideas.why: It bets that scientific AI must be embodied in a lab to close the loop from hypothesis to experiment.
